summary: Zesho Machida is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as bettō at Minobusan Okunoin Shishinkaku (attested 1990) and professor emeritus at Minobusan University (attested 1996–2001).

Zev Handel is a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology who studied at Harvard College (1988) and UC Berkeley (1992, 1998). Around 1999, he became a professor at the University of Washington.
Zhao Luo works in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied under Sen Wang and held an attested scholar post at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences in 2014.
Zhaohua Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Yang held posts at Stanford University (attested 2007) and Columbia University (faculty, attested 2018).
Zhe Ji is a religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology scholar who earned a PhD from EHESS in 2007. Ji was an associate professor at INALCO, attested from 2011 to 2017.
Zhen Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology who completed master's degrees at the University of Munich in 2005 and Lanzhou University in 2009.
Zhengyan Fan is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who served as a PhD researcher at Ghent University in 2026.

Zhenhua (1922–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tianning Buddhist College (1947) and under Yinshun (1952). Zhenhua later served as manager at Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992).

Zhihua Yao is a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Boston University under Malcolm David Eckel (~1997–2002). Yao held posts at the University of Hong Kong (~2003–2005) and CUHK (~2005).
Zhiqing Wang specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, having studied at Lanzhou University (2006–2009) and East China Normal University (2021).

Zhiru Ng is a Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies scholar who completed an MA under Luis Oscar Gómez at the University of Michigan and a PhD under Robert M. Gimello at the University of Arizona.

Zhiru Shi is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the University of Michigan (1993) and a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello. Posts include Pomona College (attested 2007–2014) and Fo Guang University (attested 2026).

Zhiyi Yang studied at Peking University, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Princeton University (PhD 2012 under Martin Kern). Yang's career in Sinology includes posts at Erlangen-Nuremberg and Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2015; Professor 2025).

Zhonghui Cui is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. Cui earned an MA from SOAS and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, where Cui was a teaching consultant (attested 2013).
Zhongpei Zhang (1934–2017) was a history, archaeology, and Sinology scholar who studied under Su Bai (~1952–1956) and served as director of the Palace Museum (~1987–1991).

Zhongxin Jiang (1942–2002) studied under Xianlin Ji at Peking University (~1960–1965). A scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, Jiang held posts at Peking University, the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978–2002), and Soka University (~1998–1999).
Zhuan Dao (1871–1943) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Tongzhi. He founded Poo Thor Jee in 1911 and Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery in 1920.
Zijie Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and served as a DC special research fellow at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science, both attested in 2015.

Zolboo Sandagjav is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at the National University of Mongolia, Delhi, Lausanne, and Bern. Career posts include Khan Bank, an internship at the UN in Geneva, and assistant lecturer at Bern (2024–2025).
Zoltán Gombocz (1877–1935) was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied at the Berzsenyi Dániel Gimnázium until 1895 and at Eötvös Loránd University from 1895 to 1900.
